name: provider
summary: Typed supplier of configuration, settings, or context behind a platform-agnostic interface.
description: Creates a provider interface plus a concrete implementation, bound in the DI container
problem: Your code needs configuration or contextual values (API keys, endpoints, prefixes, paths) but reading them directly couples you to a platform and makes testing painful. You want a small, focused interface that supplies the values, with the platform-specific retrieval hidden behind it.
appliesWhen: Code needs settings or context whose source is platform-specific (options table, env vars, config files)
Different parts of code currently access the same configuration in different ways
Tests need to inject known configuration values without touching the real source
You want a single, typed access point for a group of related values
avoidWhen: The provider would perform operations rather than supply values — that's a strategy
It would grow into a grab-bag of unrelated configuration — split into focused providers
The value is a constant that never varies by platform or environment — just define a constant
You need lazily-registered, extensible collections of items — that's a registry
examples: Add a config provider for the payment API credentials
I need a typed way to read the table prefix
Abstract where the plugin gets its API endpoint from
Create a settings accessor I can fake in tests
tradeoffs: Two files plus a DI binding. Keeps platform details out of consumers and makes configuration injectable in tests, at the cost of one more interface. Keep each provider focused on one purpose — descriptive method names, typed returns, no business logic.
outputs: A {name} provider interface with typed accessor methods to define
A DI binding mapping {implementation} to {name} in the initializer
postApply: Define descriptive, typed accessor methods on the interface (getApiKey(): string, ...)
Implement them in {implementation}, handling missing or invalid values gracefully
Create a test implementation returning known values for use in tests

name.aiHint: PascalCase, named for what it supplies, ending in 'Provider' (ApiConfigProvider, PrefixProvider). This is the interface consumers type against.

implementation.aiHint: PascalCase, prefixed with the source or platform (EnvApiConfigProvider, WordPressPrefixProvider).

initializer.description: FQCN of the initializer to register the DI binding in
initializer.aiHint: Pick the initializer that owns related bindings for this domain. If unsure, use the project's root initializer.
